candidates.title: Apollo 11 crew observes a glowing Aristarchus
candidates.quote:

some astronomers in Germany saw this

link.reason: Apollo 11's crew observing a glowing Aristarchus crater is a different event from the stories about being followed to the Moon or Aldrin's sighting.

link.difference: Frames it as a NASA catalogue centred on Aristarchus crater rather than as outgassing examples.

candidates.title: Air Force Lunex crewed moon-base plan
candidates.quote:
I

detailed plans for like an Air Force
manned mission to the moon.

link.reason: Air Force Lunex crewed moon-base plan; the nearest story, Project A119, is a different Air Force plan (a nuclear blast on the Moon), not a crewed base.

candidates.title: Reagan diary on the capacity to put 300 people in orbit
candidates.quote:

from the 80s saying I you know met with
top astronomers from from NASA

link.reason: A Reagan diary entry about meeting NASA astronomers and the capacity to put 300 people in orbit. The Reagan briefing and Reagan–Gorbachev stories are different events.

candidates.title: Classified DoD payloads as evidence of a secret space program
candidates.quote:
we know
that at Vandenberg Air Force bases there
are classified payloads that are
launched into space routinely.

link.reason: A general claim that classified DoD payloads launched from Vandenberg point to a secret space program. The Vandenberg stories are specific UFO sightings, not this program.

candidates.title: The Moon rang like a bell in the Apollo seismic tests
candidates.quote:
where it rang like a bell and they put
seismometers and they intentionally

link.reason: Same claim that the Moon rang like a bell during the Apollo seismometer experiments in 1969.
link.difference: Credits Gordon MacDonald and says the booster was crashed into the Moon on purpose.

candidates.title: GRAIL finds large lunar caverns and lava tubes
candidates.quote:

imaged the subsurface of the moon using

link.reason: GRAIL imaging of large caverns and lava tubes under the Moon's surface. The nearest stories are about Martian lava tubes and shallow lunar craters, which are different claims.

candidates.quote:

candidates.title: Francis Crick's directed panspermia
candidates.quote:
It's the reason like Francis Crick was

link.reason: Both are Jesse Michels telling of Francis Crick's directed panspermia, tied to DNA not having enough time to form on Earth.
link.difference: Adds the 100-million-year argument, Crick's book Life Itself and Carl Sagan, but does not mention the ISS fungi.

there is this particular

being fake and he will he takes the

link.reason: Jim Keller taking the 'fake' side in a debate about the Moon-landing videos. The nearest story, the Charlie Duke vs Bart Sibrel debate, involves different people.

candidates.quote:

got in touch with Dr. Hal Putoff.

link.reason: The guest's own account of contacting Hal Puthoff as a high-school student. The Puthoff stories are about his programs and other meetings, not this contact.

candidates.quote:

link.reason: The telling is about an article on the Stargate and Scanate programs, written by Puthoff according to the title or by the guest according to the quote. The Stargate program stories are about the program itself, not about a write-up of it.

candidates.title: Guest interns at the PEAR lab
candidates.quote:

with uh the pair lab. Yeah. Princeton

link.reason: This is the guest's own internship at the PEAR lab around 2003. The PEAR stories cover the lab's founding, its funding and the rebound effect, not this internship.

candidates.quote:
the hit

around 30 to 35%.

link.reason: This is the guest's analysis of hit rates in Ganzfeld telepathy trials. No story covers Ganzfeld research; the nearest are the Utts Stargate analyses, which concern remote viewing.

candidates.title: Jessica Utts' meta-analysis of the Stargate remote viewing
candidates.quote:
And she did this whole kind of
metaanalysis of Stargate and the remote
viewing stuff

link.reason: Both tell of Jessica Utts' meta-analysis of the Stargate remote-viewing data.
link.difference: Places the analysis in the 1990s.

candidates.quote:
and uh he's basically spent the last 40
years of his life working on random
event generators and trying to prove out

link.reason: This is Jahn's decades of random event generator work on mind-matter effects, with Navy interest. The nearest story is about Jahn's move from Boeing to running PEAR, which is a different claim, and the rebound-effect story is one specific finding.

so did you find any theoretical

link.reason: Speculation that Teller might be one of the physicists in a UFO legacy program; the legacy-program stories are about how insiders talk or how the program is run, not about Teller taking part in it.
